title: The full subcategory of derived-complete integral objects with constructible reductions in one common cohomological interval is closed under isomorphi
statement: Fix the global finite-field datum of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an arbitrary scheme $Y$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ and $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_Y$ on the small pro-etale site, and work in $\mathcal T=D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $P(K)$ be membership in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]: $K$ is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], each derived reduction $K\otimes_B^L(A_{E,n})_Y$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] is bounded constructible with the finite-torsion constructibility condition [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and there exist integers $r\le s$, independent of $n$, containing every reduction's cohomological support [def-weil-cohomological-support]. Then $P$ is closed under isomorphisms and is a triangulated object property: $P(0)$ holds, $P(K)$ implies $P(K[m])$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$, and every distinguished triangle $K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ with $P(K')$ and $P(K'')$ has $P(K)$. Thus the full subcategory on $P$ has the inherited triangulated structure and its inclusion into $\mathcal T$ is exact [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. No finite-type, Noetherian, dimension, or invertibility hypothesis on $Y$ is imposed.

proof.text: Identify the legacy boundedConstructibleDerivedCompleteIntegral predicate with sfIntegralConstructible pointwise. Apply sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy for the fixed auxiliary datum D and hl. integralDerivedReduction is definitionally scalarReductionDerivedExtension, and a support bound written pointwise is definitionally containment in Set.Icc. No boundedness, geometric or coefficient hypothesis is changed.

Replay the proved private completion argument of SfIntegralConstructibleTriangulated locally, without importing its cyclic coefficient-presentation aggregate. Transport an augmented Roos triangle along an isomorphism by product maps. Intrinsic completion is also isomorphism-closed. For a reflective property with unit compatible with shifts, reflection Hom bijections and triangle Hom exactness put every unit cone in the left orthogonal. An object in the right orthogonal of that left orthogonal therefore has a unit cone whose identity is zero, so its unit is invertible. Thus the property equals its double orthogonal and Mathlib makes it triangulated.

Apply this general reflection argument to the published intrinsic completion reflector and its normalized shift. The exact coefficient restriction and purCoefficientModel_predicates identify IsSfDerivedComplete with its inverse image, using the presentation counit and Roos isomorphism closure. Inverse image along the exact restriction is triangulated on an arbitrary scheme.

Define privately the uniform constructible-reduction property. Each derived reduction has its recorded exact triangulated structure, and each coefficient quotient is finite. The finite-level constructible triangulation theorem therefore proves zero, isomorphism, shift and middle-vertex constructibility. Zero has empty support. Reduction and cohomology shift comparisons translate a support interval [a,b] to [a-m,b-m], uniformly in the reduction level.

For a distinguished triangle whose outside objects have uniform reduction intervals [a1,b1] and [a3,b3], choose [min(a1,a3),max(b1,b3)]. Outside that interval the two outside cohomology objects are zero. The homology exact segment kills the middle cohomology object. This proves middle-vertex closure with a single interval for all exponents.

The integral object property is the intersection of completeness with the uniform constructible-reduction property. Mathlib intersection instances combine their isomorphism and triangulated closure. Rewrite by the equality in the first step to obtain exactly the original legacy theorem, with all universes and hypotheses unchanged. The full subcategory inherits its triangulation and exact inclusion from Mathlib.

theorem boundedConstructibleDerivedCompleteIntegral_isTriangulated
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{d}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms.{u + 2, u + 2}
      (C := completedIntegralDerivedCategory.{d, u, u} l E Y D hl)
      (boundedConstructibleDerivedCompleteIntegral.{d, u} D l hl E Y) ∧
    ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated.{u + 2, u + 2}
      (C := completedIntegralDerivedCategory.{d, u, u} l E Y D hl)
      (boundedConstructibleDerivedCompleteIntegral.{d, u} D l hl E Y) := by
  sorry
